target_customer: Gen Z users and college students paying 20 dollars a month for a money manager, debit card and savings
problem: Young people struggle to pay for college, build credit and manage money, and cannot afford a human financial advisor.
business_model: Consumer subscription (20 dollars per month) with a debit card and savings account
product_category: Gen Z financial advice and neobank

education: Dropout (school not named on the YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as a dropout and CEO of Path.

education: Dropout (school not named on the YC page)

founders.background_notes: Listed as a founder on the YC page with no bio.

technical_complexity.rationale: Consumer app with debit card issuing through a partner bank, savings and advice workflows; standard fintech engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Neobanks and Gen Z money apps were easy to replicate and the $20 monthly fee competed with free alternatives.

market_need_then: The company framed paying for college as the biggest problem in Gen Z finance (per a CB Insights profile); no independent demand data found.

branding.domain_note: Held path.me (a .me domain, not path.com); the domain now redirects to a GoDaddy for sale page.

identity.voice_and_tone: YC description is irreverent, with profanity-style wording ('don't f**k up your financial future').

branding.brand_signature: Irreverent pitch for Gen Z money advice

rebrands.why: Directories list the company as formerly ScholarMe; no source gives a date or reason

brand_strength.rationale: Name shared with a well known social app and many companies; no brand press found.

pivots.to: Path, Gen Z money manager and debit card
pivots.why: Not stated; inferred from directory listings of the former name

outcome_analysis: Path, formerly ScholarMe, sold a 20 dollar a month money manager with a credit building debit card and savings to Gen Z. A database lists five seed rounds from May 2019 to September 2021 totaling about 6.7 million dollars, but the company left almost no press, its domain is now parked for sale, and CB Insights marks it dead. No source explains the shutdown, so no failure factors are assigned.
notes: All five rounds rest on a single database (Bouncewatch, profile updated 2024-11) with no primary announcement; its stated total of 6.70M matches the disclosed amounts. Conflicts: CB Insights says 150K total with investors TEDCO, Y Combinator, Actions Capital, Pioneer Fund and MAGIC Fund; Seedtable lists a 17M seed in 2019-10, which looks unreliable and is not recorded. Round stages are all seed per Bouncewatch. path.me redirects to a GoDaddy for-sale page, so the site is dead. Competitors left empty: no dated source near mid 2019 was found; Fizz and others appear from 2021 onward. Founder education beyond 'dropout' not found.
